rulings:
### E1 — Wrong era: original step 0

The walk starts at `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (behavior-journey.ts), and this file has no wait. Its successful Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Astra calls therefore precede their recorded release dates. The recorded /v1/models bytes give Opus 5 `released: 1784851200` (2026-07-24), Sonnet 5 `1782691200` (2026-06-29), and GPT-6 Astra `1788489600` (2026-09-04). SOURCE says the catalogue was recorded 2026-09-30.

Necessary change: insert an initial wait immediately before original step 0, reaching 2026-10-01T09:00Z (`393660m` from the pinned start), before issuing credentials or sending any example. Keeping the subsequent examples at that instant is sufficient for the recorded models used. This insertion is a change to original index 0. Never excuse a pre-release success because the current handler ignores time.

### E2 — Vendor-selected catalogue ordering pinned as a customer-decided value: original step 2

`data.60.id == anthropic/claude-opus-5` pins the position in the pack's recording. The vendor's page says “Retrieve a list of all available models”; neither its example nor the spec promises model position 60. This was not decided by example setup. The source sample itself has Opus at position 0 and GPT at position 1, illustrating a shape rather than fixing a catalogue order.

Necessary change: remove the `data.60.id` equals assertion. Keep the documented list/model shape checks. If asserting Opus availability, assert membership independent of position using a decoded view or equivalent expectation, rather than a recorded positional literal. Do not pin catalogue count, created/released timestamps, or every vendor-selected model to this request.

### E3 — Request-decided model is unasserted in streams: original steps 4, 8, 12, 16

These steps only assert event-stream and DONE. Their own requests choose a model, and the vendor's stream examples return that model in the SSE JSON frames. A root-text assertion for DONE is not a semantic assertion of the returned model, even though vendor-examples.ts treats any root-path expectation as mechanically pinned.

Necessary change: add explicit assertions that the streamed JSON frame model is the requested model: Opus 5 at 4 and 16; GPT-6 Astra at 8 and 12. A raw stream assertion such as containing `"model":"anthropic/claude-opus-5"` is the minimum; a decoded frame/model assertion is stronger. Preserve the original request bodies and DONE/content-type assertions. Do not pin generated completion ids, text, usage, chunk sizes, or timestamps to the documentation sample.

### E4 — Distinct SDK image/PDF requests omitted under an incorrect identical-body claim: original steps 9 and 10; fields if the about equivalence claim is adjusted

The images page's cURL and SDK bodies are NOT equivalent. Current steps 9 and 10 correctly carry their cURL bodies and valid nonempty fixtures, but fail to represent the distinct published TypeScript/Python bodies.

Necessary changes:

* Immediately after original 9, add a published example for the image TypeScript/Python wire body (one replay represents both because those two are identical): same Opus 5 model; `messages[0].content[0].text = Describe this image in detail.`; image_url has the synthetic PNG data URL AND `detail: auto`; `stream: false`. Record this distinct body with its images-page source in doc-examples. Assert the echoed model without pinning generated description text.
* Immediately after original 10, add a published example for the PDF TypeScript/Python wire body: same Opus 5 model; text `What is the main topic of this document? Please summarize the key points.`; file `{data: <nonempty raw PDF base64>, media_type: application/pdf, filename: document.pdf}`; `stream: false`. This is not the cURL `{file_data: data:application/pdf;base64,...}` body. Record it independently in doc-examples and assert the echoed model.
* Correct supporting SOURCE/doc-examples statements that all request-language variants have identical wire bodies. Existing cURL requests must remain intact.

Fixture assessment: the PNG decodes to a real one-pixel PNG with valid IHDR/IDAT/IEND checksums; the PDF decodes to a real page tree/font/text stream and consistent xref offsets. Its declared stream length excludes the allowed separator newline. No fixture repair is required.

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions/images, Image attachments and PDF attachments.

### E5 — Published message-format examples omitted: additions immediately after original step 3

The chat-completions page publishes three distinct message-format JSON examples. They are explicit examples, not a schema field's `example` value. The tooling accepts documentation fragments, so their being message fragments rather than complete HTTP requests does not exclude them.

Necessary change: record and replay three message examples as fragments of createChatCompletion, adding only the required model/auth/message-array wrapper needed to send them:

1. Text message `{role: user, content: Hello, how are you?}`.
2. Multimodal message with text `What's in this image?` and `image_url.url` beginning `data:image/jpeg;base64,` and carrying a nonempty valid synthetic JPEG in place of the page's truncated JPEG bytes. Declare the truncation as the published placeholder with the source. Retain JPEG media type; do not silently substitute the PNG body.
3. File message with text `Summarize this document` and file `{data: <nonempty raw PDF base64>, media_type: application/pdf, filename: document.pdf}`. The page's truncated PDF bytes stand for the same valid synthetic PDF used elsewhere.

Insert these immediately after original 3; each names its own doc-example identity/source. Assertions retain only request-decided model and documented response shape, not the model's generated analysis.

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions/chat-completions, Message format/Text messages/Multimodal messages/File messages.

### E6 — Reasoning examples and output omitted; exclusions excuse a twin wire defect: original steps 11 and 12, fields

The reasoning page publishes the plaintext nonstream response, a distinct budget request, and four reasoning_details responses. The current plaintext request has no published output attached in doc-examples. All four details are excluded by a signing/encryption-key explanation. Published-example replay verifies wire shapes and types, not live cryptographic provenance. Labeled synthetic opaque strings need no provider key. Detail example 4 contains only reasoning.summary and no signature or encrypted data at all, directly contradicting its exclusion reason.

Necessary changes:

* Original 11: attach the page's complete “Response format with reasoning” sample as output to its doc-example (model GPT-6 Astra, message.role/content/reasoning, finish_reason, usage including completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens). Add expectations that visible scripted reasoning is returned with the documented field and numeric reasoning usage. Do not pin sample-generated id/text/token counts.
* Immediately after original 11: add/replay the distinct `reasoning-budget.ts` request: model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, user content `What is the meaning of life?`, `reasoning: {max_tokens: 2000, enabled: true}`; no stream field is published. Record its request in doc-examples. Assert echoed model; do not assert a generated budget amount as token usage.
* Original 12: besides E3's model assertion, assert that its scripted reasoning appears in `delta.reasoning`; DONE alone does not demonstrate the reasoning stream the source describes.
* Remove all four current notReplayed reasoning-details entries (top-level fields). Immediately after original 12, replay four separately identified examples: Anthropic nonstream reasoning.text with signature/format/index; OpenAI nonstream reasoning.summary plus reasoning.encrypted with format/index; Anthropic streamed reasoning.text with signature; OpenAI streamed reasoning.summary. Use matching published model and stream mode, and explicit synthetic fixtures for reasoning text/signature/encrypted data. Assert the documented detail types/formats/field shapes without claiming a real signature or pinning provider-generated samples. Record the four published output objects already present in doc-examples unchanged.
* Restore generic scenario/wire support when needed. The current WireTurn lacks reasoningDetails; that missing mechanism is a code defect to address in twin-world first under the architecture, not a notReplayed reason based on credentials.

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions/reasoning, Token budgets on earlier Anthropic models/Response format with reasoning/Streaming with reasoning/Preserving reasoning details across providers.

### E7 — Published advanced configuration fragments omitted: additions after original steps 16 and 19

The advanced page publishes explicit providerTimeouts and multiple-credentials examples beyond the cURL bodies already retained.

Necessary changes:

* After original 16, record/replay the providerTimeouts fragment `providerOptions.gateway.providerTimeouts.byok = {anthropic: 3000, bedrock: 5000}`. Supply only required model/messages/auth around that fragment. Retain the published timeout values. This checks admitted wire options, not elapsed real-provider latency.
* After original 19, record/replay the “Multiple credentials example” fragment: `providerOptions.gateway.byok.vertex` contains the two entries with projects `proj-1`/`proj-2`, location `us-east5`, and googleCredentials.privateKey/clientEmail; `anthropic` has the one apiKey entry. Replace the explicitly abbreviated secret strings with labeled, structurally valid throwaway credentials, declare placeholders from the page, and never use real credentials. Supply only required model/messages/auth. This represents the published arrays and their distinct fields, not the one-key body already replayed at 19.

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions/advanced, Provider timeouts/Multiple credentials example.

### E8 — Explicit published refusal rules omitted: add them immediately after original step 21

Architecture Published examples includes documented rules replayed as the refusals they cause. Current 21 represents required model, but the read pages' other concrete input refusal rules are absent. They must be recorded in doc-examples with the rule's own source and replayed, rather than left outside the measured examples.

Necessary change: after original 21 add one refusal example for each distinct rule below, using a known currently available model and otherwise valid request/credential. Each sends its stated invalid input and asserts the documented error class/envelope. Vercel's common error table documents 400 for invalid request parameters and 401 for invalid/missing authentication. Do not invent undocumented per-parameter error-code/message constants.

1. Missing `messages` (chat page Required parameters; missing model is already covered at 21).
2. Missing authorization on an otherwise valid chat request (reference Authentication/Common error codes).
3. `temperature: 3` outside 0–2.
4. `top_p: 2` outside 0–1.
5. `frequency_penalty: 3` outside -2–2.
6. `presence_penalty: 3` outside -2–2.
7. `reasoning: {effort: medium, max_tokens: 2000}` (reasoning page explicitly says they cannot be combined).
8. Unsupported `reasoning.effort: unsupported` (the page enumerates the accepted schema values).
9. Conflicting `provider.sort: cost` and `providerOptions.gateway.sort: tps` (advanced page explicitly says differing values make the request fail).
10. `response_format: {type: json_schema, json_schema: {schema: <valid object schema>}}` without required name (structured-outputs page JSON Schema parameters).
11. `response_format: {type: json_schema, json_schema: {name: example}}` without required schema (same section).

For 1 and 3–11, 400 invalid_request_error with error.message is supported by the generic documented invalid-request class; for 2 assert 401 and its documented authentication error envelope. Put exact source text in the supporting evidence and repair any handler/spec leniency that would produce success. Do not inject a scenario status fault to fake parameter validation. This ruling names original 21 for all inserted refusals; the file is a vendor example replay and is not held to the customer's single-story refusal pacing rule.

### E9 — Structured output schema, decided by the request, is not checked: original steps 6, 7, 8

These steps send a schema with five required properties and only assert model or DONE. The published output comparator sees content as a string, so an arbitrary string could pass while contradicting “structured JSON that conforms to a specific schema.” Required property names/types are decided by the caller's schema; generated product names/prices/features are not.

Necessary changes: at original 6 and 7, decode choices[0].message.content as JSON and verify it is an object with name/brand/category/description strings and price number, and any features is an array of strings. At original 8, join delta.content, parse the complete JSON (the page explicitly requires this), and verify the same schema. For 6/8 enforce the request's additionalProperties:false; 7 lacks that restriction. Use a suitable decoded answer view/data expectations, or add general parsing support if the journey cannot express it. Do not pin SteelSeries, 149.99, sample token usage, or any other generated product value. Keep every original published request unchanged.

Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/openai-chat-completions/structured-outputs, Response format/Streaming assembly.
